knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built from billable hours, so the running costs and income are covered by work that can be billed. Dividing by all paid hours, or copying a competitor's or owner's wished-for rate, does not do this.
The lesson says travel, set-up and admin time does not shrink with the size of the job, so a minimum charge covers that time for a single-item visit.

The lesson says to build the base rate from the owner's own costs and billable hours, then compare it with local evidence. A bidding-site rate, a friend's rate or a single national average with no stated basis is not a sound source.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Log one month of paid hours and billable hours to find the billable share.
